question: Does differentiating a verifier response trained on policy-dependent, selectively audited samples require a selection-propensity score term, and can omitting it reverse the outer policy-score gradient?
estimand: J(theta)=E_{z~P_theta}[r_{phi*(theta)}(z)], where phi*(theta) minimizes the clean-label squared loss under the selected distribution Q_theta(z) proportional to P_theta(z)s_theta(z).
assumptions: finite outcome space and differentiable positive P_theta and audit inclusion probabilities s_theta
conditional clean-label law is fixed with respect to theta in the main counterexample
strictly convex verifier loss with nonsingular Hessian at its minimizer
selection has positive support for both outcomes

frozen_counterexample.primary_metric: sign of d/dtheta E_{P_theta}[r_{phi*(theta)}(z)] at theta0

baselines: exact selected-distribution derivative including policy and selection scores
stop-gradient selection ablation omitting d/dtheta log s_theta
inverse-propensity reweighted verifier objective targeting P_theta
success_criterion: The implementation must exactly reproduce the rational derivatives, show opposite outer-gradient signs under the frozen misspecified verifier, and show that normalized inverse-propensity weighting targets the unselected policy distribution.
stop_criterion: If exact arithmetic or an independent finite-difference oracle disagrees, reject the claimed mechanism. A pass establishes only the mathematical counterexample, not novelty, real-system incidence, or model improvement.
confirmation_split: not applicable; fully enumerated analytic fixture
